asserts: A trace recorded under rule v1 says so in two fields, renders what the rule TOOK as a marker rather than as a value, and refuses to compare one. The `env:` field counts the environment the trace HOLDS and names the variables that were redacted out of it (`(2 vars, 1 redacted: SECRET_TOKEN)`); the `redaction:` line directly under `caps:` states the parameters of the recording -- which rule, that the store could key it and which key, whose hand last applied it -- and counts the captured values the rule took (`values redacted: 3`). The digest `0123456789abcdef` appears nowhere in any output, because a digest printed beside the name it belongs to is an offline guessing target for any short value. Every reader that PRINTS a value prints one marker: `frame` renders `token=<redacted #01234567>` and `n=<redacted #fedcba98>` -- the first EIGHT hex, enough to tell two takings apart and too few to guess from -- and renders a CONTENT hit as the text the recorder kept (`'postgres://u:<redacted>@h/db'`), because there the rule replaced a span and the rest is the program's. The readers that COMPARE values refuse instead of guessing: a taken value has no comparable value, so `watch` ends a predicate that meets only taken values at NOTHING WAS CHECKED and exit 3 rather than reporting a hit on the marker text; `flow --object` refuses a taken value's KEPT address at exit 2, since the address is real and its occupant was never recorded; and `flow --value '<redacted>'` sights nothing at all, because a literal that happens to be the marker would otherwise report every secret in the run as sightings of one value.

questions.ask: Which variables did the rule take out of this recording's environment, what rule was the recording made under, and how many captured values did it take?
expect_contains: redaction: rule v1, keyed (key 0a1b2c3d), by recorder; values redacted: 3

questions.ask: What does a reader print in place of a value the rule took whole, and in place of one it only took a span out of?
Does a predicate over a value the rule took come back as a hit on the marker text, or as a question that could not be checked at all?
May a lineage be followed through a value whose address the rule kept but whose occupant it took?
expect_contains: is redacted (by name) and has no identity or value to follow

questions.ask: Does searching for the marker text find the values the rule took?
